findings.title: Storage failures recorded as legacy duration metrics
findings.body: When Storage.Create fails, the code calls recordLegacyDuration even though the failed call was against Storage. The same mistake occurs in Update at line 129. This pollutes the legacy-store error metrics and hides storage failures from the storage metrics.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection duration recorded as storage metric
findings.body: The goroutine that calls Legacy.DeleteCollection records its result with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration. Legacy timings and errors are attributed to the storage metrics, so legacy deletecollection metrics are never emitted.

findings.title: Delete success metric uses name instead of kind
findings.body: recordStorageDuration on the success path passes `name` where every other call passes `options.Kind`. This creates a high-cardinality label (one per object name) and splits the delete metric inconsistently from the error path.

findings.title: Context built from d.Log instead of the enriched log
findings.body: In Delete, `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` is used rather than `log`, so the name, kind and method values are dropped from the context passed to storage and to the async legacy call.

findings.title: Async legacy write reuses the request context
findings.body: The goroutine derives its context from the request ctx, which is cancelled once the HTTP request returns. The legacy write is therefore often cancelled, especially under the 10s timeout, so the legacy store silently drifts. The same applies in Update, Delete and DeleteCollection. Use a context detached from the request, e.g. context.WithoutCancel. In addition, errors from the legacy writes are never logged, only counted in metrics, and the objInfo and obj are shared across goroutines.

findings.title: Tests do not verify async legacy writes and race with the mock
findings.body: The tests never wait for or assert that the legacy goroutines ran. In the failing-create case the legacy mock is set up for a call that never happens. The goroutines share a testify mock without synchronization, which risks data races and leaked goroutines after the test ends. The tests should use a sync mechanism and AssertCalled for the legacy calls.
